R7766.summary: Robert Reade, nephew and secretary of Secretary Sir Francis Windebank, who followed him into exile in Paris, writes to a cousin at court, probably Thomas Windebank. The first cipher passage weighs what to do if a proclamation goes out against Windebank: they have not enough against him to confiscate his fortune, his person would not be safe if he returned, and only His Majesty can prevent it; the second says Sir William St Ravy has done Mr Forster no good offices. Read with the Windebank cipher reconstruction DECODE R9115; 14 tokens are conjectures.
R7766.en:
Written 23 Oct 2026 (Claude Opus 5.5, translation wave v9) from reading.txt, wording unchanged: the two cipher
passages, read with the Windebank cipher reconstruction (BL Add MS 32256 f. 4, DECODE R9115; decoder key.py over
ct.txt), as running text, with the clear sentences that lead into them (in italics, as quoted in reading.txt;
the rest of the clear letter is not transcribed in the repository). The letter is in English: no translation is
needed. Spelling as the cipher spells it (goe, refusall, preuent); code groups are given by the key's word.
Holes: reading.txt's {conjectures} are written [?word] (a word the key does not give, chosen by the code's
alphabetical slot and context); [90] an unread group; letters supplied inside a word in [ ]; (ir) and the gloss
"(i.e. safe)" are reading.txt's.
